title: Widen the model: dim 512 -> 640 at depth 12
description: ASPECT_RATIO 40 -> 48, so model_dim goes 512 -> 640 with 5 heads of 128 at unchanged depth 12; one constant, nothing else touched.
reflection: NEGATIVE/wash: val_bpb 0.986873 vs baseline 0.986277, i.e. +0.0006 worse, inside the ~0.0009 noise floor. Numbers: params 71.3M -> 100.9M (+41%), FLOPs/token 3.46e8 -> 5.03e8 (+45%), total_tokens 331.5M -> 247.3M (-25%), num_steps 2529 -> 1887, steady-state MFU 38.5% -> 41.7%, peak VRAM 32.1 -> 40.7 GB. The wider model ran more efficiently per FLOP (MFU up) and still only broke even, so the extra capacity exactly paid for the 25% of tokens it cost and no more. Read together with depth (8->10: -0.0084, 10->12: -0.0027, 12->14 projected ~-0.001), this says the capacity axis is now EXHAUSTED at this time budget in both directions: we are sitting at a compute-optimal point for 300s, and buying parameters with tokens is a 1:1 trade from here. Do not spend further runs on DEPTH, ASPECT_RATIO or model_dim. The remaining runs should go to things that change quality per FLOP rather than the size of the model: MLP expansion ratio (4 -> 3 or 5), WINDOW_PATTERN (SSSL -> SSSSL/SSLL), and the untouched schedule constants (WARMDOWN_RATIO, WEIGHT_DECAY). Honest caveat: single run, and the 640-dim config inherits LRs scaled only by the 1/sqrt(dmodel) rule, so a width-specific LR retune might recover something -- but given batch size and LR were already shown flat in round 0, I would not bet a slot on it.
